## Summary

### Root Cause
The `connect` helper in `subscription.js` had an event-name mismatch in its listener lifecycle:

```js
emitter.on('data', onData);            // registered on 'data'
return () => emitter.off('close', onData)  // removed from 'close' (wrong!)
```

The listener was registered on the `'data'` event but the cleanup function tried to remove it from the `'close'` event. Since no listener was ever attached to `'close'`, `off('close', onData)` was a no-op — the `'data'` listener was **never removed**.

This is exactly why the bug report described *"every event multiple times after reconnecting"*: each `connect` call added a fresh `'data'` listener while the previous one remained attached, so every emitted `data` event was delivered to all accumulated listeners (1x → 2x → 3x...). The leaked listener count also failed the cleanup test (`n === 2` instead of `1`).

### Fix
Single smallest correct change — match the event name in `off()` to the one used in `on()`:

```js
export function connect(emitter,onData){emitter.on('data',onData);return ()=>emitter.off('data',onData)}
```

### Verification
- ✅ `npm test` passes (cleanup removes the listener, so the second `emit('data')` no longer fires `fn`).
- ✅ Reconnect simulation confirmed: connect → cleanup → reconnect yields exactly 1 delivery per emit (no duplicates) and `listenerCount('data') === 0` after cleanup.
- ✅ No tests were modified — only production code changed.
